items.title: os dev boots to healthy with a loginable seeded admin, honest DB selection, reported port shifts, and a staleness warning

requires: a free non-default port (lsof -nP -iTCP:<port> -sTCP:LISTEN empty first — dogfood skill §0) and a scratch DB path under /tmp/<run>/

⚠️ an app directory NO other runner boots, for steps[4], steps[6] and steps[7]: each writes into the directory it runs in. steps[4] bumps a tracked source file's mtime, so every other runner booting that tree reads its artifact as stale — and an `os dev` already running there is watching `objectstack.config.ts, src` and rebuilds and restarts on the change; steps[6] creates the unified default DB under .objectstack/data/ in it; steps[7] plants a legacy dev.db. Use your own worktree, or a worktree copy of examples/app-showcase (the same prescription cli.build-own-contract carries), and discard it after

for acceptance[7], the console clause, a BUILT Console: in the framework repo run `pnpm console:build` at the repo root first (`turbo run build:dist --filter=@objectstack/console`: it builds ui/apps/console in this workspace and packages/console/build-dist.sh copies that dist into packages/console/dist, which `pnpm build` never produces — it builds the Console but does not copy it). On an unbuilt tree the boot still reaches health and ready, and GET /_console/ answers 503 text/plain 'The ObjectStack Console is not built, so this server has no Console to serve at /_console/.' followed by that build remedy (packages/cli/src/utils/console.ts#createConsoleNotBuiltPlugin): record acceptance[7] blocked(environment), not a FAIL of the clause

steps: from examples/app-showcase run `objectstack dev --ui --seed-admin -p <port> -d file:/tmp/<run>/data.db` and capture the full boot log (Environment ID / Artifact / Database key-values print at boot)
poll `curl -s -m3 -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' http://localhost:<port>/api/v1/health` until 200, then GET /api/v1/ready; open /_console/ and sign in as admin@objectos.ai / admin123
stop; restart the SAME command against the SAME DB but with `--admin-password changed99`; attempt login with the ORIGINAL password (the seed is empty-DB-only and must not overwrite)
stop; in a scratch dir with NO objectstack.config.ts and no --artifact, run `os dev; echo $?` and capture the message

back in the app dir with the server DOWN, touch a src file so it is newer than dist/objectstack.json, boot with --no-compile, and capture the staleness warning block. Since #26130 `os dev` compiles by default whenever a config exists, so a boot that merely omits --compile rebuilds the artifact first and prints no warning (packages/cli/src/commands/dev.ts: the compile flag defaults on; the staleness check runs only when no compile is due)
with instance A still running, boot instance B on the same requested port and capture the '↪ server bound to port <actual> (requested <requested>)' line

run once with NONE of --database/--fresh/env-db set and no config-declared default datasource, and record the printed Database line (must be the project-anchored UNIFIED default file:<cwd>/.objectstack/data/objectstack.db); then run with `--fresh` and record the '🧪 Fresh OS_HOME' tempdir line (its DB is the SAME unified filename under the ephemeral home) and its deletion on exit

legacy compat-read: in a scratch project whose .objectstack/data holds a legacy dev.db and NO objectstack.db, boot with nothing chosen and capture both the Database line (must resolve to the legacy file — never a fresh empty objectstack.db beside it) and the one loud notice line naming that file and how to converge on the unified name

capture `echo $?` after every terminated invocation, against the expected codes: Ctrl-C/SIGINT ends a plain `os dev` with its serve child's exit code — 0 on a clean shutdown (the parent follows `code ?? 0`, packages/cli/src/utils/dev-restart.ts#ServeRestartCoordinator); a `--fresh` run's own SIGINT handler deletes the tempdir and exits 130 (SIGTERM 143); the no-config case of steps[3] exits 1

config-declared default datasource tier, for acceptance[2] (derived from the resolver source, not yet replayed live): in your own scratch project (fixtures.requires[1]), declare a NAMED sqlite datasource with a relative config.filename, e.g. `{ name: 'qa_home', driver: 'sqlite', config: { filename: '.objectstack/data/qa_home.db' } }` (the shape of the showcase's showcase-external.datasource.ts without its external block), plus a datasourceMapping rule `{ default: true, datasource: 'qa_home' }`, with every object declaring sharingModel (variants[6]). This tier reads the compiled dist/objectstack.json: `os dev` compiles it at boot by default (#26130), and `os build` first works as well. Boot with NONE of --database, --fresh, OS_DATABASE_URL, DATABASE_URL or TURSO_DATABASE_URL set, and record the Database line: it must name file: plus that filename resolved against the project root, never .objectstack/data/objectstack.db (packages/runtime/src/resolve-project-database.ts#readConfigDeclaredDefault, the rung after the explicit URL and the environment). If the boot cannot be staged, record this variant blocked(fixture) with the reason

acceptance.clause: the boot reaches health: /api/v1/health answers 200 and /api/v1/ready succeeds
acceptance.verify: the health poll flips to 200 within the probe budget; ready returns success. The console is acceptance[7], so a run with no console build scores this clause in full

acceptance.clause: --seed-admin provisions the FIXED well-known dev admin (admin@objectos.ai / admin123) loginable via the real auth endpoint, and the seed is idempotent — a later boot with a different --admin-password does NOT overwrite the existing account
acceptance.verify: login succeeds with the original credentials after the changed-password restart (flag contract: 'it acts only while no account holds the seed address and no local password login exists anywhere, never overwrites an existing account'). ⚠️ The `🔑 Dev admin: …` banner row is NOT seeding evidence: plugin-auth re-arms it on every later dev boot while the account still holds the default password (auth-plugin.ts maybeReportExistingSeedAdmin), so it reprints on boots that seeded nothing — judge the seed by the auth responses only

acceptance.clause: DB selection honors the ONE shared resolution matrix (#6469 resolveProjectDatabaseUrl, which dev maps its flags onto via resolveDevDatabase and start/migrate resolve through too): with nothing chosen, dev defaults to the PERSISTENT project-anchored sqlite file — the unified <state dir>/data/objectstack.db, i.e. .objectstack/data/objectstack.db under the project — never the historical serve default of :memory: that wipes work on restart
acceptance.verify: the printed Database key-value per variant matches the matrix, tier for tier (explicit -d url, including `-d :memory:` — SQLite's own in-memory database; env url; config-declared default datasource, staged by steps[9]; legacy dev.db/standalone.db compat-read WITH its notice line; otherwise the unified objectstack.db default) — and dev carries no fallback filename of its own

acceptance.clause: --fresh isolates OS_HOME-keyed state in an auto-deleted tempdir — and the evidence must NOT claim isolation for app-declared cwd-relative paths, which survive by documented design (#5594, e.g. the showcase-external datasource file)
acceptance.verify: the Fresh OS_HOME line names a tempdir; the dir is gone after exit; any surviving .objectstack/data/showcase_external.db is annotated as the documented #5594 carve-out, not filed as a bug

acceptance.clause: a busy requested port auto-shifts AND is reported — the actually-bound port is printed, never silently different
acceptance.verify: instance B prints '↪ server bound to port <actual> (requested <requested>)' (the IPC objectstack:listening channel exists so the parent can print the truth)
acceptance.evidence: the log line + a health probe on the actual port

acceptance.clause: a stale artifact is called out at boot: when dist/objectstack.json is older than the sources, the boot warns loudly, names the newest source and the remedy — and still boots (warn, never gate — #5148). The warning belongs to a boot that does not compile (`os dev --no-compile`); a default boot compiles first, so it has no stale artifact to call out
acceptance.verify: the '⚠ … is OLDER than your sources — this boot serves the STALE build' block prints with the newest-source path and the fix line; the server still comes up
acceptance.evidence: the warning block + subsequent healthy boot

acceptance.clause: negative: no config and no artifact exits 1 with the remedy ('Run in a directory with objectstack.config.ts, pass --artifact <path|url>, or run from the monorepo root.') — never a hang, never a silent 0
acceptance.verify: echo $? prints 1 and stderr carries the remedy line

acceptance.clause: with --ui passed, the console is served at /_console/: it serves the login page
acceptance.verify: after steps[1]'s health 200, open /_console/: it renders the console's login page, confirmed by a screenshot before any DOM read (RUNNER rule 1). It needs a BUILT Console (fixtures.requires[2]); on an unbuilt tree /_console/ answers 503 text/plain 'The ObjectStack Console is not built, so this server has no Console to serve at /_console/.', and this clause is recorded blocked(environment), never a FAIL

negative: a dev boot that wipes an existing dev DB when the user chose nothing (a regression to the historical :memory: serve default) is the FAIL the persistent default exists for

a dev boot that ACCEPTS the retired in-memory (mingo) engine — `--database-driver memory`, `OS_DATABASE_DRIVER=memory|mingo|in-memory`, or `-d memory://` / `mingo://` — is a FAIL: it is not a boot store (it refuses every tenant-scoped read, so a data read answers 503). The flag value is refused while the flags parse (oclif's allowlist message, exit 2); the env spelling is refused BEFORE any Database line prints, exit 1; the URL is refused by the serve child after the parent's Database line, exit 1 — each naming `--fresh` and `:memory:` except oclif's own allowlist line

a boot that silently opens a fresh empty objectstack.db beside an existing legacy dev.db — or reads the legacy file WITHOUT printing the notice — is a FAIL: the compat-read exists so an established dev environment never looks like data loss
an auto-shifted port that is not reported (URL printed for the requested port while the server bound elsewhere) is a FAIL
variants: unified default: file:<cwd>/.objectstack/data/objectstack.db (persistent, imposed only when nothing else chosen)
--fresh (ephemeral tempdir OS_HOME; same unified filename under it; implies --seed-admin)
OS_DATABASE_URL / DATABASE_URL / TURSO_DATABASE_URL env (env wins over the default)
-d :memory: (SQLite's own in-memory database — the replacement for the retired in-memory engine; nothing persists across restarts)
--database-driver memory / OS_DATABASE_DRIVER=memory|mingo|in-memory / -d memory:// or mingo:// → REFUSED (the retired in-memory engine; see the negative for where each is refused and what it names)

config-declared default datasource (the project config's default home wins over the unified default) — authored as a NAMED datasource plus a datasourceMapping rule { default: true, datasource: NAME } (readConfigDeclaredDefault); a datasource literally named `default` is refused by defineStack as reserved for the host's primary, and a mapping rule naming 'default' is declined, so neither can stand for this variant. The scratch stack's object must declare sharingModel (e.g. 'private'): without one the boot's compile refuses the stack on the error rule security-owd-unset (packages/lint/src/validate-security-posture.ts#SECURITY_OWD_UNSET) and `os dev` exits 1 with 'Compile failed — fix errors above before starting dev server' (packages/cli/src/commands/dev.ts)
legacy compat-read: an existing dev.db / standalone.db when no objectstack.db exists (resolved WITH one loud notice line; probe order objectstack.db → dev.db → standalone.db)
source: packages/cli/src/commands/dev.ts#resolveDevDatabase (resolveDevDatabase — dev's ONE resolution seam onto the shared matrix, carrying no fallback filename of its own; the persistent-default rationale; --fresh coverage note #5594; seed-admin idempotency contract; IPC bound-port report; #5148 staleness warning + rebuild-restart coordinator)

packages/runtime/src/resolve-project-database.ts#resolveProjectDatabaseUrl (#6469 resolveProjectDatabaseUrl — the shared priority matrix explicit → env → config-declared default datasource → unified <state dir>/data/objectstack.db, with a retired in-memory driver selection refused ahead of every rung (retiredMemoryEngineMessage), the state-dir order homeDir/OS_HOME/<projectRoot>/.objectstack/~/.objectstack, and the legacy dev.db/standalone.db compat-read with its loud notice)

items.title: os build's own contract: no computed value in the exit slot, located errors for schema and author-time rule failures, artifact + stats output, warnings never flip the exit

requires: a scratch copy of a known-good app config (scaffolded blank app or a worktree copy of examples/app-showcase) so deliberate breakage never touches shared fixtures. A plain-literal object added to it carries the package's namespace prefix in its name: an unprefixed one is refused for NAMESPACE_PREFIX first, and that refusal masks the break steps[2] makes and the advisory steps[5] reads
knownGaps: no spec docblock or ADR states the --json payload shape of os build or os validate; the one governed element is the conversion notice both publish under conversions (packages/spec/src/stack-provenance.ts#stackConversionsOf). So acceptance[3] follows the code at base 7697ddcf94 (the emitJson payloads in compile.ts and validate.ts): the two commands spell the verdict (success / valid) and the finding list (issues / errors) differently, and build's own failure exits differ among themselves — the author-time rule and --strict-body failures carry issues, while the post-lowering schema parse, the container-name and the picklist refusals carry errors. A refusal at load carries its message and code only: packages/cli/src/utils/format.ts#errorCodeFields copies code and httpStatus, so the zod issues the STACK_SCHEMA_INVALID ledger row says that error carries ('issues carries the zod issues structurally', packages/spec/src/api/error-code-ledger.zod.ts) reach neither payload. Which spelling is canonical is unruled: score acceptance[3] on the warnings/conversions parity, and record both payloads as they are

steps: on the clean config run `os build; echo $?` and capture the summary (metadata stats, Artifact path/size)
run `os build --json` and capture the success payload

break the schema: give one field an impossible shape (e.g. delete its type) and run `os build; echo $?` — capture the located Zod error. Make the break on an object authored as a PLAIN LITERAL handed to defineStack: ObjectSchema.create() parses at import (data/object.zod.ts), so the same break inside a helper-authored object (ObjectSchema.create / Field.*) dies at 'Loading configuration…' with the raw Zod issue array (path [fields, body, type], no object name) and never reaches the located 'defineStack validation failed … objects.0.fields.body.type' block this clause scores

break an author-time rule: author a flow whose Approval node approver expression does not parse (the #4409 worked example that once built green while os lint rejected it) and run `os build; echo $?`. Keep the config's `requires: ['automation', 'triggers']`, which the scaffolded blank app and the showcase both declare: when the flow carries an auto-launch trigger (record_change, schedule, time_relative or api) and `requires` lacks either token, defineStack refuses the stack at load (packages/spec/src/stack.zod.ts#validateTriggerCapability) and the build never reaches the author-time rule this step scores
re-run both failing builds with --json and capture the failure payloads

restore the config and add one UNDECLARED authoring key (the #3786 advisory class) where it is still an advisory: object, field, report and enable shapes are CLOSED, so an unknown key ON a field is a hard refusal (exit 2 out of defineStack, exit 1 'Validation failed … unrecognized_keys' under strict:false) — that is clause 2's territory, not this one. The advisory survives only at a nested strip-mode site, e.g. inside a field's object-form visibleWhen ({ dialect: 'cel', source: …, qaUndeclared: 1 }), on a RAW field object of a plain-literal object: written inside ObjectSchema.create() the key is stripped by that helper's own parse, with no advisory under either defineStack mode (build exit 0, the key silently absent). acceptance.evidence: the collected exit codes with the --json and human paths labelled separately, plus the repeat runs showing each code is stable

items.title: os migrate: bare command is a read-only plan, apply is safe-by-default, re-runs are idempotent, and --json exits 0 on success (#4873)

requires: a scratch app + persistent sqlite DB whose base schema was synced by one prior `os dev` boot (plan itself defers DDL since #3917, so the tables must pre-exist), e.g. -d file:/tmp/<run>/migrate.db
knownGaps: no pin scores a clause of this item at its layer (RUNNER rule 6, a pin scores only the layer it drives), so the item carries no automated ref. Every clause's oracle is the CLI's own output or exit code. packages/cli/src/utils/format.exit-code.test.ts calls emitJson / emitText in-process (unit): it shows that the success path leaves process.exitCode alone and that a duration can no longer reach the exit-code slot (#4873). That is unit-layer evidence for acceptance[2], never its pass: acceptance[2] is scored on the `echo $?` collected after each subcommand's --json success. automated may return when a pin spawns `os migrate … --json` and asserts the shell's exit code

steps: boot the scratch app once with `os dev -d file:/tmp/<run>/migrate.db` so the base schema exists; stop it

add a new field to one object in the config and `os build`; run bare `os migrate` twice — both runs must print the SAME pending add-column plan and mutate nothing. On a DB an `os dev` boot synced, that plan also carries create_table entries for the lifecycle-classed objects (seven at 5b14b7f3, QA run #24551): the dev boot kept them in its telemetry sibling (ADR-0057 §3.6), and a plain `os migrate` mirrors a non-dev boot, which has no sibling, so it plans them against the primary. Expect them beside the add-column, or run plan and apply under NODE_ENV=development (or OS_TELEMETRY_DB naming the sibling) so the one-shot boot provisions it as the syncing boot did (schema-migrate.ts, #22579)
run `os migrate plan --json; echo $?` and capture the payload ({ database, managedTables, total, changes, pending })

run `os migrate apply --yes; echo $?` and capture the applied list; then `os migrate plan` again and `os migrate apply --json --yes; echo $?` — the idempotent re-run. On the showcase (it declares federated showcase_external objects, which have no managed table) expect the PARTIAL reading: plan prints 'No drift over the N object(s) this plan examined — but M of T declared object(s) were NOT examined … PARTIAL plan', and the JSON re-apply answers message in_sync_partial with composition.coverage.reasons.federated > 0. Plain in_sync is the answer only for an app whose every declared object was examined
remove a field from the config + `os build`; run `os migrate apply --yes` WITHOUT --allow-destructive (the drop must be SKIPPED with a warning), then with `--allow-destructive --yes` (applied)

with the dev server booted and holding the DB, run `os migrate apply --yes; echo $?` (expect the busy refusal, exit 1, without --force) and `os migrate plan` (proceeds with a warning — a plan writes nothing either way)
run `os migrate apply --json` WITHOUT --yes on a pending change: the payload must say confirmation_required with the pass--yes hint and mutate nothing
the #4873 pair: on the scratch DB run `os migrate recorded-by --json; echo $?` and `os migrate resume --json; echo $?`

the #4873 --json sweep over every subcommand: read the set from the CLI itself, never from a list typed into this item. `os migrate --help` prints it under COMMANDS (oclif pattern strategy: one default-exported Command per non-test file in packages/cli/src/commands/migrate/, index.ts being the bare command); capture that list. For each listed subcommand the steps above did not already run, run its dry-run form `os migrate <name> --json; echo $?` on the scratch DB, adding only what that subcommand's own `os migrate <name> --help` USAGE line marks required (unmapped-columns takes --object <name>). audit-key-material (#26772) is in the set and takes the same flags as audit-mail-bodies (--apply, --yes, --force, --json), so its dry run is the probe. ⛔ The one exception: duplicates (#8928) is ALWAYS JSON on stdout and has NO --json flag, so run it bare (`os migrate duplicates; echo $?`) and never feed it --json, whose oclif Nonexistent-flag exit 2 is not a #4873 violation (deep coverage at cli.migrate-duplicates-inventory). A subcommand added later joins the sweep through the --help list, with no edit here, unless it too lacks --json

acceptance.clause: bare `os migrate` is the dry-run plan and NEVER mutates: boot-time DDL is deferred and the artifact seed suppressed (#3917), so two consecutive plans report identical drift and the physical schema is unchanged
acceptance.verify: the two plan outputs match; a schema dump (or third plan) after them equals the first
acceptance.evidence: the two plan outputs + schema check

acceptance.clause: plan --json emits the declared shape and exits 0
acceptance.verify: payload carries database/managedTables/total/changes/pending; echo $? is 0

acceptance.clause: #4873 exit-code honesty: EVERY migrate subcommand with --json exits 0 on success — never the elapsed-ms leak (recorded-by/resume once passed timer.elapsed() into the exit-code slot, so the shell saw duration & 0xFF: a different bogus nonzero on every successful run)
acceptance.verify: echo $? after plan/apply/recorded-by/resume --json successes, and after every other subcommand the sweep step read from `os migrate --help` (duplicates run bare), is exactly 0; the CliExitCode 0|1 type now makes the mistake a compile error
acceptance.evidence: the captured `os migrate --help` COMMANDS list + the collected exit code per listed subcommand

acceptance.clause: apply is safe-by-default: a destructive change is SKIPPED with an explicit warning until --allow-destructive, then applied with it — both sides captured
acceptance.verify: the drop appears under skipped (with the re-run hint) on the first apply and under applied on the --allow-destructive run

acceptance.clause: idempotent re-run: after a successful apply there is nothing left to apply and the re-run exits 0 — and the in-sync claim is scoped to what was EXAMINED: on the showcase, whose federated objects are never diffed, plan prints the PARTIAL warning (not the 'in sync' success line) and apply --json answers message in_sync_partial carrying composition.coverage (unexaminedObjects > 0, reasons.federated > 0); only an app with no unexamined object answers in_sync / 'Physical schema is in sync with metadata — nothing to migrate.'
acceptance.verify: on the showcase: the post-apply plan prints the PARTIAL warning naming the unexamined count; the JSON re-apply payload is { applied: [], skipped: [], created: [], message: 'in_sync_partial', composition: { coverage: { unexaminedObjects > 0, reasons.federated > 0 } } } and echo $? is 0 (apply.ts / plan.ts in-sync early returns, schema-migration-plugins.ts coverage). An app with nothing unexamined answers message 'in_sync' and the in-sync success line instead. ⛔ in_sync_partial on the showcase is NOT a failed migration — it is the declared honest reading of a partial reconcile

acceptance.clause: a busy database refuses apply (exit 1) without --force, while plan proceeds with only a warning — the read/write asymmetry is deliberate
acceptance.verify: apply against the server-held DB exits 1 naming the occupancy; plan against the same DB completes with the busy warning

acceptance.clause: --json is non-interactive: a mutating apply without --yes reports confirmation_required + the hint and performs NO change
acceptance.verify: the payload says confirmation_required, hint 'pass --yes'; a follow-up plan still shows the pending change

negative: an apply that performs a drop WITHOUT --allow-destructive is the FAIL the safe-by-default split exists for
exit 0 from a refused (busy) apply, or ANY nonzero exit from a successful --json run, is a FAIL — exit codes are the load-bearing CI contract here

items.title: objectstack verify: verdict vocabulary is closed, exit is nonzero exactly on failure verdicts, and the inconclusive split (needs-fixture/skipped) never fails the run

requires: examples/app-showcase as the verified app (its config is the stock target)
knownGaps: no stock fixture ships a GUARANTEED-failing app, so the exit-1 side of the hardFailures mapping must be staged (point --app at a scratch config engineered to produce a fidelity gap or 5xx create) — record how it was staged in the evidence rather than skipping the side silently

no pin scores a clause of this item at its layer (RUNNER rule 6, a pin scores only the layer it drives), so the item carries no automated ref. packages/cli/src/commands/verify-tenancy-posture.test.ts asserts resolveVerifyMultiTenant, the exported decision, under the real tenancy-posture resolver; its own docblock says it is 'not an end-to-end `os verify` invocation'. That is unit-layer evidence for acceptance[4], never its pass: acceptance[4] scores the posture run's payload (multiTenant) or its loud error. automated may return when a pin runs os verify under a walled OS_TENANCY_POSTURE and reads that payload

steps: from examples/app-showcase run `objectstack verify --json > report.json; echo $?`
assert every results[].status in report.json is one of the six declared verdicts, and recompute the summary counts from results[] (they must reconcile)
recompute hardFailures = createFailed + readFailed + fidelityGaps (+ rls holes when --rls ran) from the report and compare to the exit code
run `objectstack verify --rls --json; echo $?` (the RLS proofs boot a SEPARATE fresh stack by design — unique-constraint collisions with the fidelity phase would silently skip objects)
run `OS_TENANCY_POSTURE=isolated objectstack verify --json` and capture either multiTenant:true in the payload or the hard boot error — never a quiet single-org run (#5262)
stage the fail side per the knownGap and capture `echo $?` (expect 1) alongside the failing report
capture the human-format run too (`objectstack verify`) and check the ✓/✗ banner agrees with the recomputed hardFailures

acceptance.clause: the verdict vocabulary is closed: every per-object status is exactly one of verified | fidelity-gaps | create-failed | read-failed | skipped | needs-fixture
acceptance.verify: scan results[].status in the JSON report against the six-member union in packages/verify/src/verify.ts

acceptance.clause: exit code is nonzero EXACTLY when hardFailures > 0, where hardFailures = createFailed + readFailed + fidelityGaps + rlsHoles — recomputed from the report, never trusted from the banner
acceptance.verify: echo $? is 0 when the recomputed sum is 0 and 1 when it is positive (the staged failing run)
acceptance.evidence: exit codes paired with recomputed sums

acceptance.clause: the inconclusive split is honored: a 400 VALIDATION_FAILED on the auto-derived record is classified needs-fixture (a fixture gap, not a platform finding) and does NOT fail the run; a 5xx is create-failed and DOES
acceptance.verify: needs-fixture and skipped counts are excluded from hardFailures in the report vs exit-code comparison; the classification comment in verify.ts is the contract
acceptance.evidence: report excerpt showing needs-fixture objects on an exit-0 run

items.title: os test: a Quality Protocol suite is validated at LOAD, executed against a booted app, and its verdict is the exit code — capture/interpolation thread state, an unevaluable assertion FAILS

requires: a free non-default port and an ephemeral boot: `pnpm dev -- --fresh -p <port>` from the repo root (showcase + --seed-admin; dogfood skill §0). It needs a built workspace and NO console build: the root dev chain runs scripts/check-dev-prereqs.mjs first, which refuses an unbuilt workspace and prescribes `pnpm build`, then boots the showcase, which on an unbuilt console warns that it has no Console to serve and names `pnpm console:build` (packages/cli/src/utils/console.ts#formatConsoleDistMissingWarning). Every step here drives REST and the CLI, never /_console/, so that warning is no blocker

a session token for the data steps — POST /api/v1/auth/sign-in/email with the seeded admin (admin@objectos.ai / admin123) and read `.token`; pass it as `os test --token <token>` (the CLI sends it as `Authorization: Bearer`)

the shipped fixture suite examples/app-showcase/qa/platform-smoke.test.json — the repo's only Quality Protocol suite, authored so `os test`'s DEFAULT glob (`qa/*.test.json`) finds it from that directory with no argument
a scratch directory with its own qa/ for the negative and variant probes — deliberately broken suites are STAGED per run, never committed, so the repo's own suite stays green
knownGaps: `run_script` has no adapter branch and fails by name (`Unsupported action type in HttpAdapter: run_script`) — the variant sweep records ONE refusal and that is the honest verdict, not a fixture gap to work around. The other seven members execute since #7848; the five record-shaped ones did not until then (see `negative`), so a sweep transcript predating that fix shows five 404s and is not comparable

the record action types resolve the Data Protocol mount from the server's own `/discovery` (`routes.data`) since #7983, so a deployment that sets `crud.dataPrefix` IS reached; what remains out of reach is `api.apiPath`, which moves the discovery document itself out from under the probe (measured: `{apiBase}/discovery` 404s, and `/.well-known/objectstack` reports the DISPATCHER's `/api/v1/data`, not the REST mount). Against such a host the adapter falls back to the convention and says so — it names the mount it addressed, the probe that failed and the remedy, on the warning AND on every 404 — and those steps must still be written as `api_call`. The fixture boot is stock, so neither case bites here

scenario SELECTION is by tag only: `os test --tags a,b` runs the scenarios carrying at least one listed tag (any-of, exact, case-sensitive — commands/test.ts `selectScenariosByTags`), counts the rest as deselected — not run, never counted as passed — and without the flag the whole glob runs. Preconditions SKIP rather than select: a scenario whose `requires.params` variable is unset or empty in the `os test` process, or whose `requires.services` entry the target's discovery does not declare enabled and available, is skipped with its reason (core runner.ts `judgeRequirements`), counted apart and never passed. The fixture suite declares no `requires`, so the green path exercises no skip; a skip probe must be STAGED — a scenario requiring a service the stock showcase boot does not declare available (`search` is one: nothing in the open framework registers that slot) — and an all-skipped run exits 0, or 1 under --fail-on-empty

steps: boot the app: from the repo root `pnpm dev -- --fresh -p <port>`; poll `curl -s -m3 -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' http://localhost:<port>/api/v1/health` until 200

mint a token: `curl -s -X POST http://localhost:<port>/api/v1/auth/sign-in/email -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -H 'Origin: http://localhost:<port>' -d '{"email":"admin@objectos.ai","password":"admin123"}'` and read `.token`

the green path on the DEFAULT glob: `cd examples/app-showcase && os test --url http://localhost:<port> --token <token>; echo $?` — capture the whole transcript including the `Found N test suites.` line and the summary
prove the teardown ran: list `GET /api/v1/data/showcase_category` before and after and confirm the row the run created is gone (the run leaves the fixture exactly as it found it)
prove the run repeats: execute the same command a second time and confirm it is green again with no leftover row — a suite that only passes once is a suite whose teardown is decorative

stage the negative probes in a scratch dir's qa/: (a) a suite with `steps` misspelled as `stpes`, (b) a suite asserting `data.status equals degraded` against /api/v1/health, (c) a suite asserting `contains` over `data.nope`, a path the health response does not carry. Run `os test 'qa/*.test.json' --url http://localhost:<port>; echo $?` and capture all three refusals in one transcript

prove the malformed suite never ran from the transcript: its refusal carries no `Scenario:` line (the load-site refusal precedes execution), while the two OTHER staged suites still print their '📄 Running suite:' heading and their `Scenario:` lines after it. The server log is no oracle here: the stock dev boot writes no per-request access line, so 'no request in the log' holds whether the suite ran or not

teardown-after-failure: stage a scenario that creates a record, captures its id, then fails a deliberate assertion, with a teardown that deletes `{{id}}`; run it and confirm via the API that the record is gone despite the red verdict

variant sweep: stage one scenario per TestActionTypeSchema member (8) and run them in one suite; record each member's own verdict and the exact error text of every refusal — no member inferred from a sibling
zero-match glob: `os test 'qa/nothing-matches-*.test.json' --url http://localhost:<port>; echo $?` and record BOTH the message and the exit code
glob discipline (#7363): `os test 'qa/**/*.test.json'` from the app dir — it must complete in seconds and find the same suite, never the multi-minute walk that preceded the lazy resolver
persona check: re-run the green suite with NO --token and record which scenario survives (health) and which fails (the data roundtrip, HTTP 401)

Since #7848 that is a DECLARED posture (stated in `--help`, opt out with `--fail-on-empty`, which exits 1) rather than an accident, but the default is unchanged and so is the trap: a CI job wired to `os test` with a typo'd path still reports success forever unless it passes the flag. the five record-shaped action types (`create_record`, `read_record`, `update_record`, `delete_record`, `query_records`) **round-trip** against a stock server, and an **HTTP 404** from any of them is now the regression this clause names. They answered 404 until #7848 — `HttpTestAdapter` built `${baseUrl}/api/data/:object` where the server serves `{apiPath}/data/:object` with `apiPath` = `/api/v1`, and `update_record` issued PUT where the route is PATCH. Both are fixed and the prefix is derived from `RestApiConfigSchema` + `CrudEndpointsConfigSchema` rather than written down, so this cannot regress by a literal drifting. Re-measured 2026-08-12 on showcase, one scenario per member with no shared setup: 7 of 8 execute and assert, `run_script` refuses by name
variants: api_call — the only action type that reaches the real API surface (target is a path or absolute URL; `payload.method`/`payload.body` shape the request)
wait — local, no HTTP; resolves `{ waited: <ms> }` from `payload.duration`
create_record — POST {apiPath}/data/:object → 201 `{ object, id, record }` (404 before #7848)
read_record — GET {apiPath}/data/:object/:id → `{ object, id, record }`; the id comes from `payload.id`
update_record — PATCH {apiPath}/data/:object/:id with `payload.id` peeled off the body (it addresses the record, it is not a column write); issued PUT to a route that has no PUT sibling before #7848
query_records — POST {apiPath}/data/:object/query with the QueryAST as the body → `{ object, records }`

the adapter was repaired, which this item's own `negative` clause declared to be a revision rather than a silent green (#7848). Item 1: the five record-shaped action types now round-trip against a stock server — the `${baseUrl}/api/data/:object` literal became a prefix DERIVED from the two schemas RestServer itself resolves from (RestApiConfigSchema `apiPath ?? {basePath}/{version}` + CrudEndpointsConfigSchema.dataPrefix), and `update_record` PATCHes where it used to PUT a route that has no PUT sibling. items.title: os migrate meta replays the spec migration chain over authored sources and PRINTS the mechanical edit list the retirement messages prescribe — by default it rewrites no source file, and --write rewrites in place exactly the edits it can prove, held to a re-run of the chain; its --out snapshot is schema-valid, replay is idempotent, and a below-floor --from is refused

requires: a scratch copy of an authored source tree, and a SECOND fresh copy for the --write leg: --write (#9591) rewrites the authored files in place, so it never runs on the checked-out app. The default run (no --write) writes nothing but --out (commands/migrate/meta.ts: 'By default it writes no source file'), and the --stored arm is a read-only preview until --apply. --stored --apply IS a real write too — to this deployment's sys_metadata ROWS, not to files
authored sources deliberately carrying retired spellings from the previous major, so the chain has something to report
knownGaps: Constructing sources that carry the OLD spellings requires authoring against a retired surface, which the current schemas refuse at parse. Author the fixture files as raw text (they are the input a real upgrader has on disk — files written before the retirement, which is exactly why they do not parse now); do NOT try to produce them through the current schema. If a retired spelling cannot be reconstructed for a sampled entry, record that entry as blocked(fixture) rather than declaring the chain clean over it.

The registry carries entries for both the shipped major and the next one. Conversions for the NEXT major may be staged but not yet reachable through a released --from/--to pair; record which sampled entries were actually exercised.

--write writes a site only when it can trace it to ONE object or array literal in ONE project file whose value matches the loaded one; every other site is REFUSED with a kind from a closed set (computed, helper, spread, shared, outside-project, mismatch, injected, unspellable, layout, unattributed, entangled — packages/cli/src/utils/authored-source-codemod.ts CodemodRefusalKind) and listed under 'left for you to apply by hand' with its reason. Plant the retired spellings as plain literals the config module reaches (directly, or through a relative import or a define* helper) so each is traceable. A planted site the run lists as refused, with a kind from that set and a reason naming the blocker, is the contract working, not a fail of the write clause — record its kind and re-plant that entry as a plain literal; a refused site with no kind or no reason is a finding.

steps: enumerate the migration registries and record their sizes: packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/{retired-defs,retired-keys,semantic}

collect the command's advertised contract from the SHIPPED retirement messages: grep the spec for the house sentence they carry — `Run \`os migrate meta --from <N>\` to list the mechanical edits for existing sources; \`--write\` applies the ones it can prove, and you apply the rest by hand.` (shared text in packages/spec/src/shared/retired-key.ts, reworded class-wide by #9529 and given its `--write` clause by #9591) — and record which majors are named. ⚠️ The sentence promises a LIST by default and an in-place write only for the edits --write can prove: the default run is judged on the listing being complete and honest, the --write run on writing exactly the provable edits and nothing else

copy an authored source tree to a scratch dir and plant retired spellings sampled from the retired-keys registry (at minimum one ui/ key and one data/ key); record a per-file checksum of the scratch tree BEFORE the run
run `os migrate meta --from <previous major>` and capture stdout + the exit code
confirm every planted spelling appears in the printed `Applied <N> mechanical change(s):` block as `<path>: <from> → <to> (<conversionId>)`, naming the successor the registry declares
re-checksum the scratch tree and confirm every authored file is byte-identical — the run's only file write is --out

re-run with `--out <snapshot>.json`, read the snapshot back, and confirm the run states its schema verdict honestly: `Migrated stack is schema-valid` when it is, and, when the migrated stack still fails the schema, the `Migrated stack does not yet pass schema validation — <n> refusal(s) left after the chain. Resolve them, then run \`os validate\`:` warning, followed by each refusal (packages/cli/src/commands/migrate/meta.ts#printSchemaVerdict)

idempotence: replay a CANONICAL source — one carrying no shape the 17 → 18 chain converts; the tree the WRITE MODE leg wrote is one, while the stock showcase tree is NOT (three edge-branched decisions omit `mode`, so flow-decision-mode-inclusive-explicit lists three edits over it) — over a real range — `os migrate meta --from 17` (--to defaults to 18, CHAIN_TERMINUS_MAJOR: the higher of the runtime's PROTOCOL_MAJOR and the highest major the registries carry a step for, 18 on both counts since PROTOCOL_VERSION moved to 18 (#22215); the run's `Chain:` line prints both) — and confirm NO `Applied <N> mechanical change(s):` block and exit 0; the step-18 semantic advisories are still listed (every hop lists its semantic entries unconditionally), so `Nothing to migrate …` is NOT the expected line here. Then run the identical `--from <previous major>` command on the planted tree a second time and diff the two stdouts with the verdict line's elapsed-time stamp (`(<n>ms)`) normalized away — it is a timing, not report content. Separately record the EMPTY-RANGE answer: `--from 18` (range 18 → 18, no step) prints `⚠ No migration step exists for protocol 18 → 18, so this run replayed nothing — that is not a finding that the metadata is canonical.` — never the canonical success line
run it with a --from BELOW the supported floor and capture the MigrationFloorError path (`Cannot migrate from protocol <N>: the chain's support floor is <F>`)
run it with --json where supported and check the exit code in the same way #4873 required of every other migrate subcommand

confirm the semantic-only entries behave as ADVISORIES: they are reported under `<N> manual change(s) require your judgment:` with their why/verify text, never silently 'fixed' (a semantic change has no mechanical rewrite by definition)

WRITE MODE (#9591): run `os migrate meta --help` and record the --write line. Then, on a SECOND fresh scratch copy carrying the same planted spellings, keep a byte copy of the tree and run `os migrate meta --from <previous major> --write`; capture stdout + the exit code. Read the `Wrote <N> of <M> mechanical change(s) into <K> file(s):` block (each site `:<line> <path> (<conversionId>)`), any `<N> mechanical change(s) left for you to apply by hand:` block (each with its `not written [<kind>]: <reason>`), and the closing `Re-ran the chain over the written sources: …` line. Diff the tree against its byte copy: the changed files are exactly the files the block names, plus, when the run owed the manifest's declared protocol range an edit (a tree declaring engines.protocol '^17'; the stock showcase declares '^18'), the config file that the separate 'Rewrote the declared protocol range, so the load admits protocol N:' block names with its line. That rewrite is not one of the chain's M changes, so the 'Wrote …' block never lists it, and `--json` reports it as write.range, apart from write.written[]. Each hunk sits at a listed site, and every other byte (comments, formatting, key order) is unchanged. Then, over the WRITTEN tree: re-run `os migrate meta --from <previous major>` without --write (no written site is still listed under Applied; the semantic advisories are listed exactly as before), run `--write` a second time (it writes nothing: `--write: the chain made no mechanical change here, so no file was written.`), and run `--write --json` on a third fresh copy (exit 0; the payload's `write.status` is `written` and `write.written[]` names each site with its file and line)

acceptance.clause: every planted retired spelling is REPORTED in the printed mechanical-edit list, with the successor the registry declares — the listing the retirement messages prescribe is complete, for each sampled entry
acceptance.verify: locate each sampled entry in the `Applied <N> mechanical change(s):` block (`<path>: <from> → <to> (<conversionId>)`); an entry left unlisted while a shipped message prescribes this command for it is a FAIL naming that entry — the prescription is then a dead end
acceptance.evidence: the printed block, with each sampled entry located in it

acceptance.clause: WITHOUT --write the authored sources are UNTOUCHED — the default run's only file write is the --out snapshot. This is the shipped contract, not a defect: the source rewrite is opt-in (--write, acceptance[7]), and the command's own docblock says 'By default it writes no source file'
acceptance.verify: per-file checksums of the scratch tree before and after the runs made without --write: every file byte-identical, and the only new or changed path is the --out target when --out was passed
acceptance.evidence: the before/after checksum pairs + the --out path

acceptance.clause: the --out snapshot is the migrated stack, and the run reports its schema verdict honestly rather than claiming success over outstanding manual work
acceptance.verify: read the snapshot back and reconcile it against the printed applied set; check the success/warning line agrees with `schemaValid` in the --json output for the same input
acceptance.evidence: the snapshot, the verdict line, and the --json schemaValid field

acceptance.clause: replay is IDEMPOTENT: replaying a canonical source over a range that CONTAINS steps lists zero mechanical edits and exits 0, and two identical runs print the same thing — while an EMPTY range (--from equal to the --to default, 18) is answered as an empty range ('⚠ No migration step exists for protocol N → N …'), never as a green 'already canonical' verdict over a check that never ran
acceptance.verify: the canonical-source replay `--from 17` (default --to 18) over a canonical source (the written tree, never the stock showcase — see the step) prints no `Applied <N> mechanical change(s):` block (only the step-18 advisories) and exits 0; `--from 18` prints `⚠ No migration step exists for protocol 18 → 18, so this run replayed nothing — that is not a finding that the metadata is canonical.` (meta.ts printEmptyRangeAnswer) and NOT `Nothing to migrate — …`; the two identical planted-tree runs diff empty once the elapsed-time stamp is normalized. An upgrader re-runs this command, and a chain reporting fresh work on clean input cannot be trusted
acceptance.evidence: the canonical-replay output + exit code, the empty-range output, and the diff of the two identical-run stdouts

acceptance.clause: a --from below the supported floor is REFUSED loudly (MigrationFloorError) rather than silently doing a partial or wrong replay
acceptance.verify: non-zero exit and a message naming the floor and the supported range; a silent no-op here would leave an upgrader believing they had migrated

acceptance.clause: semantic-registry entries are surfaced as ADVISORIES the operator must act on — reported, never silently marked handled
acceptance.verify: the output distinguishes mechanically-listed entries from advisory ones; a run that reports 'migrated' over a semantic change nobody applied is the dangerous direction
acceptance.evidence: the output, with the two classes identified

acceptance.clause: the exit-code honesty rule holds here as on every other migrate subcommand: --json exits 0 on success (#4873)
acceptance.verify: `os migrate meta --json ...; echo $?` is 0 on a successful run

acceptance.clause: --write rewrites the authored sources IN PLACE for exactly the mechanical changes it can prove, and for nothing else (#9591): each planted spelling traced to a literal is written at its site, each one it cannot trace is listed with a refusal kind and reason, no semantic advisory is written, every byte outside a written site is unchanged, and the write is held to a re-run of the chain over the written sources — so the written tree no longer carries the converted spelling, and a second --write has nothing to do
acceptance.verify: the WRITE MODE step: the `Wrote <N> of <M> mechanical change(s) into <K> file(s):` block names a file and line for each traced planted spelling, N plus the by-hand count equals M (the Applied count of the dry run over the same input), and the run closes with `Re-ran the chain over the written sources: no mechanical change remains.` (or `only the <n> change(s) left above remain.`), which ends ` The declared protocol range now admits protocol N.` when the run rewrote the range, and exits 0; the diff against the pre-run byte copy touches only the named files, only at the named sites: the 'Wrote …' block's, and the range block's one site when the run owed the range an edit (meta.ts printRangeOutcome); the re-run without --write lists no written site under Applied and the same semantic advisories; the second --write prints `--write: the chain made no mechanical change here, so no file was written.`; `--write --json` exits 0 with `write.status` `written`. ⛔ A write the re-run disagrees with must come back `restored` with exit 1 and every file at its old bytes, never half-converted (meta.ts writeSources) — a reported `written` over a tree the re-run still converts is a FAIL
acceptance.evidence: the --write stdout and exit code, the before/after tree diff, the re-run stdout, the second --write line, and the --json write block

negative: a retirement message prescribing `os migrate meta --from N` for a spelling the chain does not LIST — the prescription is then a dead end, and the author who follows it is worse off than one who was told nothing
a listed edit whose declared successor ALSO does not parse (pointing the author at a second retired name)
a run WITHOUT --write that mutates the authored sources is a FAIL of the untouched-sources clause — the rewrite is opt-in

a --write that changes any byte outside a listed site (a site the 'Wrote N of M mechanical change(s) into K file(s)' block lists, or the declared protocol range its 'Rewrote the declared protocol range' block names), writes a semantic advisory, drops a planted spelling from both its written and its by-hand list, or reports the write done while the re-run over the written tree still converts a written site, is a FAIL of the write clause
a below-floor --from that silently no-ops and exits 0
a replay from the target major that reports changes, or two identical runs whose stdouts disagree
`Migrated stack is schema-valid` printed while manual changes are still outstanding — the same dishonesty as reporting 'migrated' over a semantic change nobody applied

items.title: The documented newcomer verification loop closes on a FRESHLY SCAFFOLDED project: os validate passes and the Console actually paints at /_console/ — the seam between the scaffold item and the showcase boot item
personas: a brand-new developer following the published docs, with no prior project (content/docs/getting-started/quick-start.mdx carries the validate/dev check but no create-objectstack command; the scaffold line is the scaffolder's own published usage)

requires: a scratch dir and network access for `npx create-objectstack` (same prerequisite as cli.scaffold-first-run)

for an unreleased candidate (steps[0]'s pre-release route): a localhost npm registry with NO upstream for @objectstack/* and create-objectstack, exactly as cli.scaffold-first-run's pre-release variant prescribes — the container image carries none (QA run #24551 installed verdaccio@6 into the run dir with npm and packed the public workspace packages, ~1 min)
knownGaps: This item deliberately does NOT re-prove what two existing items already cover. The scaffold→install→validate→build→artifact-boot chain belongs to cli.scaffold-first-run (automated by .github/workflows/scaffold-e2e.yml); the console-on-a-populated-app half belongs to cli.dev-boot-contract, which drives examples/app-showcase. What is untested is the SEAM: the Console rendering against a freshly scaffolded BLANK project — one object and no seed data. Score only the seam; cite the two siblings for the halves.

A blank scaffold DOES have a loginable identity out of the box: `seed-admin` is default-ON in dev (commands/dev.ts: flags['seed-admin'] ?? true, 'Default: on (idempotent — it acts only while no account holds the seed address and no local password login exists anywhere, never overwrites an existing account)'), so bare `objectstack dev` seeds admin@objectos.ai / admin123 on an empty DB and the banner prints the credentials. Clause 4 therefore scores whether the newcomer can COMPLETE the documented visual check with that identity, not whether one exists. Still do not import showcase credentials.

the scaffold serves the console its OWN install put in node_modules. On the PUBLISHED path that is @objectstack/console from the registry at the scaffold's version, not this repository's workspace Console build: the seam is then the published console against a blank project, and a console change merged in ui/apps/console but not yet released is not exercised (cli.dev-boot-contract on examples/app-showcase is where the workspace build is served). Under the PRE-RELEASE variant it is the candidate's own packed @objectstack/console — its dist is the copy packages/console/build-dist.sh makes of ui/apps/console's build, so build it (`pnpm console:build`) before packing or the tarball carries no dist/index.html — and an unreleased console change IS exercised. The run record names which path it took

steps: scaffold a fresh project the way the scaffolder's published usage spells it — quick-start.mdx itself carries no create-objectstack command: `npx -y create-objectstack@latest qa-console-first-paint; echo $?` (no -t flag — the docs never pass one; for an unreleased candidate use cli.scaffold-first-run's pre-release variant). The scaffolder installs ITSELF (pnpm when found, npm otherwise) and the docs prescribe no separate install — ⛔ do not add a trailing `npm install`: it fails on a pnpm-installed scaffold (17.6.0 and 17.7 alike)
run the documented gate: `npx os validate; echo $?`

run `npm run dev` — the scaffold's OWN script, which is what a newcomer reaches for once the scaffold has installed; the scaffolder's Next steps name the package manager that installed it, so a pnpm install prints `pnpm run dev` (packages/create-objectstack/src/index.ts), the same script — and probe http://localhost:3000/_console/. Port 3000 is the default; a runner confined to a port range exports OS_PORT and passes the port through the scaffold's own script (`npm run dev -- -p PORT`), then probes that port — the same substitution applies to step 4's `npx os dev --ui -p PORT`
load the console in a browser and record what a newcomer actually sees: does the shell render, and is there any identity they can sign in with?

stop; run the documented spelling `npx os dev --ui` and probe /_console/ again — the two must agree (see clause 3; `--ui` is a forwarder for a serve-side flag that is already default-on, so this is a no-op equivalence check, not a divergence hunt)
capture the boot log for both invocations

acceptance.clause: `npx os validate` passes on the untouched fresh scaffold — the documented gate is green on the thing the documented scaffolder just produced
acceptance.verify: exit code 0; any refusal on a pristine scaffold is a P1 finding (the first command in the docs fails on the first project)

acceptance.clause: the Console PAINTS at /_console/ on a fresh blank scaffold under the DOCUMENTED command (`os dev --ui`) — not merely on the showcase
acceptance.verify: the console shell renders (not a 404, not an empty body, not a stack trace); confirm against the served HTML and a rendered screenshot, since a 200 that paints nothing is the failure this clause exists to catch
acceptance.evidence: status + screenshot of the rendered console

acceptance.clause: the scaffold's OWN `dev` script serves the console with NO extra flag — `npm run dev` (bare `objectstack dev`) reaches /_console/ exactly as `os dev --ui` does
acceptance.verify: probe /_console/ under both invocations; both must serve. The console is default-ON downstream: `dev` spawns `serve` (packages/cli/src/commands/dev.ts) forwarding `--ui` only when set and never forwarding `--no-ui`, and serve declares `ui` with `default: true, allowNo: true` (packages/cli/src/commands/serve.ts) — so an unflagged `dev` lands on serve's own default. `--ui` on `dev` is a no-op forwarder, which is what content/docs/deployment/cli.mdx means by 'Force Console UI on (already on by default in dev)'. A difference between the two invocations is the FAILURE here, not the expectation

acceptance.clause: a newcomer can complete the documented visual check, or the run states precisely what stops them — the docs promise 'create a record, watch an action show/hide, confirm the nav and filters' on this project
acceptance.verify: attempt the documented visual check: sign in with the seeded dev admin and create a record on the scaffold's object (a 201 that reads back). The action/nav half ('watch an action show/hide, confirm the nav and filters') has NOTHING to act on here — a blank scaffold ships no app and no action — so it is a stated LIMIT of this item, recorded as not-applicable and never as a FAIL or a PASS; the in-console continuation that authors an app and lands it in the launcher is studio-authoring.first-run-loop (it does not author an action either). If no identity exists to sign in with on a blank scaffold, that is the finding — record it rather than substituting showcase credentials
acceptance.evidence: what the newcomer sees, including any sign-in wall, plus the record create + read-back

negative: the console 404s on a fresh scaffold while working on the showcase — a first-run-only failure that every showcase-based test is blind to
`npm run dev` and `os dev --ui` disagreeing about /_console/ — that would mean the forwarding in dev.ts or the default in serve.ts changed, and the newcomer path silently regressed
a future edit giving `dev` its own `ui` default of false, or forwarding `--no-ui`: either would strand the newcomer, and neither would be caught by any showcase-driven item
os validate refusing on a pristine scaffold
a console that returns 200 and paints nothing (white screen) — 200 is not the oracle here, the rendered DOM is
source: content/docs/getting-started/quick-start.mdx ('How you verify' — `npx os validate` and `npx os dev --ui`, then open http://localhost:3000/_console/)

packages/create-objectstack/src/templates/blank/package.json#scripts.dev (scripts.dev = `objectstack dev`, with no --ui — correct, see the chain below — re-pointed #18104: objectstack is a VALUE in this manifest and never a key; scripts.dev is the key pair this item reads)
packages/cli/src/commands/serve.ts (`ui: Flags.boolean({..., default: true, allowNo: true })` — the console is default-ON here; `--no-ui` is the off switch)

packages/cli/src/commands/dev.ts + (dev declares `ui` with NO default and forwards `...(flags.ui ? ['--ui'] : [])` — it only ever ADDS the flag, never forwards --no-ui, so an unflagged dev inherits serve's default-on)
content/docs/deployment/cli.mdx ('--ui | Force Console UI on (already on by default in dev)') and ('--ui / --no-ui — Toggle Console UI at /_console/ (default on)')
packages/create-objectstack/src/template-registry.ts#TEMPLATES (TEMPLATES = { blank } only; RETIRED_TEMPLATES named for a named refusal)
sibling item cli.scaffold-first-run (scaffold→install→validate→build→`os start --artifact`→health/ready; automated by .github/workflows/scaffold-e2e.yml)
sibling item cli.dev-boot-contract (os dev --ui + /_console/ sign-in, driven against examples/app-showcase)
sibling item studio-authoring.first-run-loop (the in-console authoring loop, once the console is reachable)

history.change: new — angle-5 (docs claims) probe of the published first-run. Covers a real seam between two existing items: cli.scaffold-first-run boots the scaffold headless via `os start --artifact`, cli.dev-boot-contract drives the console against the fully-populated showcase, and nobody drives the console against a fresh BLANK scaffold — where there is no seed data and no seeded admin unless one is requested. Checked and CLEAN on three questions the sweep raised: no doc anywhere in content/docs/ prescribes a retired template (`todo`/`compliance`/`content`/`contracts`/`procurement`), every documented invocation is a bare `npx create-objectstack my-app` resolving to the only catalog entry, and `npm run validate` is the same binary as `npx os validate`. Source-checking the chain disproves it — dev.ts forwards `--ui` only when set and never forwards `--no-ui`, serve.ts declares `ui` `default: true`, and cli.mdx states outright that the console is 'already on by default in dev'. The bare script is CORRECT; `--ui` on `dev` is a no-op forwarder. Clause 3 accordingly asserts the two invocations AGREE, and a difference is the failure

two corrections from run #21845. Read at base 9753d163: packages/console ships only dist/ (files [dist, README.md, CHANGELOG.md]), and `pnpm console:build` builds ui/apps/console and copies it there. No clause changed

The run's third line (the published scaffold resolves 18.1.0) is already knownGaps[2]. Re-read at base e4ba846f. No clause changed

items.title: os doctor: every check emits an attributed row, an unparseable posture is an ERROR not a swallow, ledger rows print under every posture, the ✓ is withheld when the read was incomplete — and the two monorepo-anchored scans announce a named skip in a user app instead of blessing a tree they never walked

requires: a scratch blank scaffold (`npx -y create-objectstack@latest qa-doctor -t blank` + install — the same provisioning cli.scaffold-first-run drives) as the USER-APP shaped tree; the monorepo-vs-user-app split is load-bearing for the monorepo-anchored-skip clause and BOTH cwds must be run — the skip rows exist only outside this checkout, and the rows they stand in for only inside it
a scratch copy of the config for the deliberate config findings (orphan view, circular lookup pair, unreferenced object) — breakage never touches shared fixtures
a writable .objectstack/installed-packages/ in the scratch tree, so an unreadable ledger entry can be staged per run
knownGaps: no stock fixture ships a config with an orphan view / circular lookup / unused object, so the config-analysis rows must be staged; record the staged shapes in evidence rather than skipping the rows silently. The staged config must still LOAD: when defineStack refuses it, doctor reports a 'Config load' warning row and skips the whole config-analysis block, so the three rows never print
the config-analysis block runs only `if (configExists())` (doctor.ts) — a bare directory exercises the environment rows alone; run both shapes and label which produced which rows

steps: baseline: from the untouched scaffold run `os doctor; echo $?` and `os doctor -v; echo $?` — capture both full reports (the environment rows print first: the unconditional Node.js, pnpm, TypeScript, Dependencies, Git, Environment files and Package-authored scheduled work, with whichever finding-only rows are live in their places — then the extended checks, then, when a config loads, the config block, which opens with its Platform protocol row)

stage the config findings in the scratch copy: a view whose object does not exist (orphan), two objects whose lookup fields point at each other (circular), and one object nothing references (unused); run `os doctor` and capture the three warning rows — then restore and capture the three ✓ rows (Dependencies / Object usage / View integrity). The untouched blank scaffold is NOT that clean baseline: its starter object — the template's blank_note, renamed to the project's namespace (qa_doctor_note for the qa-doctor scaffold) — is referenced by no view, app or flow (its src/views, src/apps and src/flows barrels are empty), so findUnusedObjects warns on it and the report never reaches its healthy line. Add one view over it to the scratch copy (e.g. views: [{ name: 'qa_doctor_note', object: 'qa_doctor_note', list: { columns: ['title'] } }]) before the clean run. Stage the orphan as a WELL-FORMED view container whose name equals its object key and whose object does not exist, e.g. views: [{ name: 'qa_missing', object: 'qa_missing', list: { columns: [...] } }]: the default defineStack load accepts it and all three checks run. A malformed view body (e.g. a single view's viewKind/config keys on a container) is refused by the default load, and doctor then prints '⚠ Config load  Could not load config for analysis (config checks skipped)' and runs none of the three — a staging fault, not a doctor finding; defineStack(…, { strict: false }) loads any shape, and is the route when the staging itself needs a shape the closed schema refuses

unparseable posture: `OS_TENANCY_POSTURE=isolatd os doctor; echo $?` — the Tenancy posture ERROR row must print naming the variable and the allowed set, the REST of the report must still run, and the exit must be 1 (#5382: report-not-refuse, resolved OUTSIDE the config-analysis try at doctor.ts, row pushed)

env provenance: put the same bad posture in a .env FILE (not the shell) and re-run — the finding must still fire (#5387 dotenv cascade) and the Environment files row must attribute the value to the file that supplied it

ledger: write .objectstack/installed-packages/broken.json holding non-JSON; run `os doctor` with NO posture set (default `single`) and capture the Installed packages row; then with a valid config and OS_TENANCY_POSTURE=isolated, confirm the run does NOT print the 'Unique scope ✓' success line while that entry is unreadable
exit split: on a warnings-only run capture `echo $?` (expect 0, '⚠️  Environment is functional' summary); on the posture-error run expect 1 ('❌ Some critical issues found' + the collected fix lines)

the monorepo-anchored skips: in the scaffold — which has NO packages/spec/src — capture verbatim the two informational rows 'ℹ Test coverage Skipped — no packages/spec/src in this directory (monorepo-only check)' and 'ℹ Deprecations Skipped — no packages/spec/src in this directory (monorepo-only check)', then re-run with -v and capture the '→ Looked for <cwd>/packages/spec/src and found nothing to walk. …' detail line under each. Assert the ABSENCE of three lines in the SAME transcript: '✓ Test coverage All *.zod.ts files have matching tests', '✓ Deprecations No @deprecated tags found', and the '@objectstack/spec Not built' warning row — that probe is now gated on <cwd>/packages/spec/package.json (doctor.ts), so in a user app the row is correctly not printed at all. Then run the same command from a monorepo checkout for the counterpart transcript: there the '→ Checking…' step lines, the scan's own ✓/⚠ rows and '✓ @objectstack/spec Built' all print

acceptance.clause: every environment check emits its own row, and the finding-only rows appear exactly when their finding is live — Node.js, pnpm, TypeScript, Dependencies, Git, Environment files and Package-authored scheduled work (ON or OFF, #17396) are unconditional; @objectstack/spec prints only where <cwd>/packages/spec/package.json exists (#10679), NODE_ENV only while NODE_ENV is unset (#5673), Tenancy posture only on an unrecognized value (#5382), and Installed packages only on a ledger failure or a skipped entry (#5429); once a config loads, the config block opens with its own Platform protocol row (✓ when the declared engines.protocol covers the installed platform, ⚠ when checkProtocolVersionGap reports a gap) — and -v adds the fix/detail lines without changing the verdicts
acceptance.verify: both transcripts carry one row per check through renderHealthCheckResult (doctor.ts); the unconditional rows are the run body's results.push calls that no condition guards — Node.js, pnpm (pnpmCheck), TypeScript (typescriptCheck), Dependencies, Git (gitCheck), Environment files (environmentSourcesCheck) and Package-authored scheduled work (packages/cli/src/commands/doctor.ts#scheduledWorkCheck) — and the four finding-only rows are pushed under their guards: the spec workspace (gated on the package.json probe), nodeEnvCheck, postureReading and installedPackageLedgerChecks (which returns [] on a clean ledger); the Platform protocol row is printed by the config block from checkProtocolVersionGap, not pushed among them; the -v run differs only by detail lines
acceptance.evidence: the paired scaffold transcripts, plus the same pair from a monorepo cwd — a conditional row that is absent and a row that was dropped read identically in one transcript alone

acceptance.clause: #5387 env provenance: doctor resolves the same .env* cascade os serve reads, and the Environment files row names WHICH source supplied each value — the files are never silently merged into process.env
acceptance.verify: the.env-staged posture still produces the finding, and the Environment files row attributes it to that file rather than the shell (environmentSourcesCheck at doctor.ts; pinned by doctor-env-provenance.test.ts — cite its pass as the attribution oracle, drive the CLI for the row itself)

acceptance.clause: #5382 posture honesty: an unrecognized OS_TENANCY_POSTURE is an ERROR row naming the variable — never swallowed by the config-analysis catch as 'Could not load config for analysis' — the rest of the report still runs, and the summary owns exit 1
acceptance.verify: the isolatd run prints the Tenancy posture error row, later report sections still print after it, and echo $? is 1 (posture resolved once at doctor.ts, outside every try; exit via the hasErrors summary)

acceptance.clause: #5429 ledger independence: installed-package ledger rows print under EVERY posture including the default `single` — an unreadable entry under .objectstack/installed-packages/ is its own row whether or not a config loaded and whether or not any posture was set
acceptance.verify: the broken.json run with no posture set carries the Installed packages failure row (readInstalledPackageEntries called unconditionally at doctor.ts; posture-independence pinned by doctor-ledger-posture-independence.test.ts + doctor-ledger-read-failure.test.ts)

acceptance.clause: the unique-scope ✓ is WITHHELD when the ledger read was incomplete: under `isolated` with an unreadable ledger entry, the 'Unique scope' success line must NOT print — a ✓ over an unexamined ledger is a false PASS (#5412/#5413/#5644)
acceptance.verify: the isolated+broken-ledger run prints no 'Unique scope … No unconfirmed installation-wide uniques' line (gated on ledgerReadingIsComplete at doctor.ts), while the same run with the entry removed prints it
acceptance.evidence: the two isolated-run transcripts diffed on that line

acceptance.clause: config-analysis rows both ways: the staged orphan view, circular lookup and unused object each produce a warning row naming the offender, and the restored config, plus one view over the blank scaffold's starter note object, produces the three ✓ rows
acceptance.verify: detectCircularDependencies / findUnusedObjects / findOrphanViews rows (called at doctor.ts) name the staged shapes; the clean run prints the 'Dependencies', 'Object usage' and 'View integrity' successes — an Object usage ⚠ naming the starter note object on that run is the missing staging view, not a doctor finding

acceptance.clause: exit contract: 1 exactly when any ERROR row exists; warnings alone exit 0 under the '⚠️  Environment is functional' summary — warnings never flip the exit
acceptance.verify: echo $? per run matches the summary branch taken (process.exit(1) only under hasErrors, doctor.ts)
acceptance.evidence: exit codes paired with summary lines

acceptance.clause: the two monorepo-anchored scans report whether they RAN, and the ✓ is reachable only from the arm that did (#10679 — this clause was the EXPECTED-FAIL at revision 1 and is now an ordinary pass): findMissingTests and findDeprecatedUsages return a MonorepoTreeScan (doctor.ts) whose `scanned: false` arm is taken in any app without <cwd>/packages/spec/src. There doctor prints neither ✓ and neither '→ Checking…' step line; each check KEEPS its name column and prints an informational skip naming the reason, and -v adds the directory doctor resolved and looked for. The skip goes through printInfo, never printWarning — withholding a false ✓ must not manufacture a false ⚠ (rationale)
acceptance.verify: in the scaffold (no packages/spec/src anywhere) the report carries 'ℹ Test coverage Skipped — no packages/spec/src in this directory (monorepo-only check)' and the same row for 'Deprecations' (monorepoTreeSkipNotice, printed); the two ✓ lines and their step lines are absent; and the skip rows move neither hasErrors nor hasWarnings, so the summary branch is the one the other rows earned. The -v run adds '→ Looked for <cwd>/packages/spec/src and found nothing to walk. …' under each. From a monorepo checkout the scanned arm still runs and its ✓/⚠ findings still print — the fix scoped the check, it did not delete it
acceptance.evidence: the verbatim skip rows from both the plain and the -v scaffold run, an `ls packages/spec/src` refusal from the same cwd, and the monorepo-cwd transcript showing the scanned arm still reporting

negative: an unrecognized posture reported only as 'Could not load config for analysis' with exit 0 is the exact #5382 regression the placement fix closed
a 'Unique scope ✓' printed while an installed-packages entry was unreadable is a false PASS — worse than a missing check, because it stops the operator looking further
warnings flipping the exit to 1, or an error row exiting 0, breaks every CI wrapper that gates on doctor

a '@objectstack/spec Not built' WARNING in a user app is a REGRESSION of #10679, not a note to record: outside this checkout there is no such workspace, and that row used to flip every stock scaffold to '⚠️ Environment is functional but has some warnings' while prescribing `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec build`, a command that cannot succeed there. The probe is now gated on <cwd>/packages/spec/package.json (doctor.ts) and the honest report in a user app is no row at all

a ⚠ rather than a ℹ on the Test coverage / Deprecations skip rows is the same false-signal class inverted: nothing is wrong in an app that has no packages/spec/src, and routing the skip through printWarning would end every healthy user app's report on 'Environment is functional but has some warnings'

requires: a scratch app + persistent sqlite DB whose base schema was synced by ONE prior `os dev` boot (the same recipe cli.migrate-plan-apply-json uses), e.g. -d file:/tmp/<run>/dup.db — the app config must declare an org-scoped object with an autonumber (or unique) field

direct SQL seeding after that boot (sqlite3 CLI or a node better-sqlite3 one-liner): one identifier value held by a row with organization_id NULL AND a row with organization_id '<org>' (the cross-partition duplicate); the same value twice WITHIN '<org>' on a second identifier (the excluded repeat); and two _objectstack_sequences rows for the same object/field — one __global__ tenant, one org-scoped (the live condition). The stock showcase declares ONE org-scoped identifier (showcase_field_zoo.f_autonumber), so the second identifier the within-partition repeat sits on must be declared in the scratch app (another autonumber, or a field carrying unique). Drop that field's partitioned unique index first — uniq_OBJ_organization_id_FIELD (an autonumber defaults to unique: 'organization'; the SQL driver names the index in packages/drivers/driver-sql/src/schema-drift.ts#buildIndexName) — or the repeat's second insert is refused. After the drop, `os migrate plan` over the same database reports that index as an index_mismatch drift (actual '(absent)'): the staging's own footprint, not a finding of this item
knownGaps: ORDERING IS LOAD-BEARING: do NOT boot the dev server again between seeding and scanning — a #8686-repairing boot backfills organization_id = NULL, which is exactly the evidence this report inventories (the command's own header calls the evidence perishable). The duplicates command itself boots read-only (deferSchemaDdl + readOnlyProbe) and is safe to run any number of times

the memory driver does NOT lack a raw-SQL seam — `InMemoryDriver.execute()` logs `Raw execution not supported in InMemory driver` and returns null, which is exactly the SHAPE the seam resolver tests for, so the no_sql_seam refusal was dead code for it (a clean `duplicates:[]` exit 0 instead, #10677). The refusal now keys on whether a seam returns a RESULT SET rather than on whether `execute` exists. ⛔ That branch can no longer be driven from a CLI boot: the in-memory engine was retired as a boot store, so a memory-driver scratch config (`--database-url memory://…`) now answers `{error: 'boot_failed'}` exit 1 with the retirement message before any seam exists. The no_sql_seam clause is satisfied by the seam-double pin instead — `packages/cli/src/commands/migrate/duplicates.null-seam.test.ts` runs the real command over a driver whose `execute` answers no result set — and its pass is the evidence.
