items.title: os plugin build enforces the manifest at the packaging boundary: an invalid manifest is refused with located errors, `bundled` is the one packaging strategy (the retired `manifest-deps` is refused at the manifest, a native addon is refused by name), and the compiled manifest the artifact carries is readable back
personas: plugin author (local shell, scratch plugin directory)

requires: a scratch plugin directory OUTSIDE the repo tree holding objectstack.plugin.json (the filename os plugin build reads — NOT objectstack.config.ts), an entry at src/index.ts, and a package.json declaring at least one real, pure-JavaScript runtime dependency that the entry actually imports. ⛔ Without a genuinely imported dependency there is nothing to inline and the bundled clause is unscoreable — a bundle that merely lacks an external import would then be a fixture defect read as a product pass
esbuild resolvable from that directory — os plugin build refuses with its own named error when it is not, which is a fixture failure rather than a clause verdict

a second scratch directory for the refusal probes, so a bad manifest never overwrites the good one. The native-addon probes need no compiler: the build refuses a `.node` file by its path and never loads it, so any bytes in a file named addon.node will do, and a dependency that 'declares a node-gyp build' is a hand-written node_modules/<name>/ holding a package.json, an index.js and a binding.gyp
knownGaps: os plugin publish CANNOT complete locally: after extracting the artifact manifest it requires a cloud token and posts to <server>/api/v1/cloud/packages. Only its PRE-NETWORK legs are scoreable here — artifact discovery in cwd, manifest extraction, the id/version refusal, and the unsigned-artifact notice. Record blocked(environment) for anything past the auth step; the cloud control plane is not part of this checklist's fixture set

the SERVER-side mirror of the identity refusal — POST /api/v1/packages/publish answering 400 PACKAGE_MANIFEST_INVALID when id or version is missing (packages/rest/src/package-routes.ts) — is deliberately not scored here: it needs a deployment composing the `package` service, and one without it answers 404 with the 'composes no `package` service' message, which is not a failure of anything. Score it from the api lane if a marketplace-capable deployment is available

the artifact is a gzipped ustar with mtime pinned to 0 and entries emitted in sorted path order, so identical inputs produce byte-identical archives — which is also why a stale artifact from an earlier run is indistinguishable from a fresh one by name alone. Check for the artifact's ABSENCE after every refusal probe in a directory that never held one

the native-addon refusal reads what the build can SEE: a `.node` module in esbuild's graph, a bundled package that declares a node-gyp build or ships a `.node` file, and a `.node` file under assets/. An addon loaded at run time from an absolute or computed path outside every bundled package is invisible to it, and is not scored here — the artifact would fail at load on a host that lacks it

steps: in the scratch plugin dir, run `os plugin build` on the GOOD manifest (id, version, name, an imported dependency in package.json, no `packaging` key) → capture the full output: the Loaded line, Artifact, Plugin, Files, Integrity entries, Size, sha256

copy the good project into the second scratch dir, set `packaging: "manifest-deps"` in ITS objectstack.plugin.json and build there → capture the output, the exit code, and the directory listing after it

extract the good artifact (gunzip + tar) and read its FILE LIST and its entry bundle. Expect exactly objectstack.plugin.json, dist/index.mjs and SIGNATURE (plus any assets/ the project carries) — no package.json and no lockfile — and expect the declared dependency's code inlined in dist/index.mjs with no import or require of it surviving
read the compiled manifest out of the artifact (the objectstack.plugin.json entry inside the archive) and compare it to the authored one: expect the authored keys plus `main` and an `integrity` map

run `os plugin publish` against the good artifact with no token → capture the output up to and including the auth refusal; then run it against an artifact whose compiled manifest lacks a version → capture that refusal

REFUSAL probes, each in the second scratch dir, each followed by a check that NO artifact file was written: (a) objectstack.plugin.json that is not valid JSON; (b) a manifest missing `id`; (c) a manifest whose `version` is not semver; (d) a manifest with `id: ""` — which the reverse-domain rule on manifest.id (MANIFEST_ID_PATTERN) refuses at safeParse with a located error; (e) a manifest with no `main` and no src/index.* entry candidate. Then, on a VALID manifest: (f) an entry that imports ./native/addon.node; (g) an entry that imports a node_modules dependency declaring a node-gyp build (binding.gyp), beside a pure dependency it also imports; (h) an assets/bin/addon.node beside an ordinary asset

run `os lint` on a scaffold config whose manifest declares NO engines range → capture the finding (rule, severity, path, fix); then run it on a bare metadata fragment that declares no manifest at all → confirm the rule does NOT fire there

teardown: delete both scratch directories. ⚠️ Do not re-run a refusal probe in a directory an earlier build wrote an artifact into — a leftover file reads exactly like a fresh one, and the no-artifact half of every refusal clause is then unscoreable

acceptance.clause: an invalid manifest is REFUSED at build with LOCATED errors and no artifact: an unparseable objectstack.plugin.json is refused by name ('Cannot read objectstack.plugin.json in <cwd>'), and a manifest that parses as JSON but fails ManifestSchema is refused with the per-key Zod errors printed — each exits nonzero and leaves no .osplugin behind
acceptance.verify: run probes 6a-6c and read stdout plus the exit code; then list the directory and confirm no artifact was written. ⛔ Score the exit code and the absence of the file together — a refusal that prints and still writes an artifact is the shape that ships a broken plugin
acceptance.evidence: each refusal's full output with its exit code, plus the directory listing taken after it

acceptance.clause: identity is guarded at the SCHEMA, with located errors for every shape: `id` and `version` are required by ManifestSchema (an absent one fails safeParse with a located error), a non-semver version fails its SemVer regex, and `id: ""` fails manifest.id's reverse-domain rule — a located Zod error ('Invalid package id ''. A package id (`manifest.id`) is written in reverse-domain notation, like …'), not the build's post-parse 'must declare both "id" and "version"' guard. That guard (build.ts) is now unreachable from a manifest that passed safeParse; an empty id never reaches it, and it is not scored
acceptance.verify: probes 6b, 6c and 6d, each read as its OWN located refusal under 'objectstack.plugin.json is invalid:' — 6b the missing key, 6c the version regex, 6d the reverse-domain refusal naming manifest.id with the received '' — each exiting nonzero with no artifact. 6d printing 'must declare both "id" and "version"' instead would mean the schema rule regressed. Collapsing the three into one 'it refuses' observation cannot tell which rule answered
acceptance.evidence: the three refusals side by side, each with its exit code

acceptance.clause: `bundled` is the ONE packaging strategy (ADR-0025 v2 §3.3): the build inlines every dependency the entry imports except the host-provided `@objectstack/*` packages and packs neither package.json nor a lockfile — and the retired `packaging: 'manifest-deps'` is REFUSED at the manifest, a located error under 'objectstack.plugin.json is invalid:' naming `packaging` and telling the author to delete the key, exiting nonzero with no artifact
acceptance.verify: step 3 for the bundled half — the file list AND the inlined dependency must both hold, since a missing package.json alone could come from any archive change; step 2 for the refusal half, read with its exit code and the directory listing. ⛔ A manifest-deps build that writes an artifact, or prints the Loaded line with `packaging: manifest-deps`, is the retired fork answering again

items.title: autoMigrate off|safe: a dev boot self-heals ONLY the safe-categorized drift and reports each applied op, `off` (the driver default) and NODE_ENV=production never touch the schema, and a unique index the stored rows already violate is blocked, never auto-applied

requires: a SCRATCH app copy (a scaffolded blank app or a minimal stack beside a symlinked node_modules) whose config declares a NAMED sqlite datasource (e.g. qa_main — defineStack refuses a datasource named `default`: 'that name is reserved for the host's primary datasource, and every boot refuses a stack that declares it') with a file DB under the run's scratch directory, routed as the primary by datasourceMapping: [{ default: true, datasource: 'qa_main' }]; deliberate metadata edits and direct writes to the STOPPED scratch file stage the drift, so shared fixtures are never touched
a debug-readable boot log for every boot — the safe-apply evidence is the driver's own [schema-drift] lines

for the config-declared arms: the datasource's driver `config` is where `autoMigrate` is authored (sqlite.zod.ts; the same key on postgres/mysql); for the injected arm: a boot with NO config-declared datasource, whose fallback default datasource gets `autoMigrate: 'safe'` from the CLI only when isDev
knownGaps: the duplicates-BLOCKED leg (the ADR-0120 D4 duplicate pre-flight on a unique create_index: rows that already violate the declared key → the op BLOCKED, category destructive, an applyLimit naming the conflicting group, no index created) needs duplicate rows under a newly declared unique field — stageable only by writing them into the STOPPED scratch sqlite file before the boot that declares `unique: true`. The block is unit-pinned (sql-driver-25031-blocked-unique-apply-limit.test.ts), but that pin runs initObjects with autoMigrate unset and never boots a safe driver over the blocked op, so 'never auto-applied under safe' is the hand-staged leg's; a run may cite the pin per RUNNER rule 6 for the rest, and must record WHICH route each half rests on. Since ADR-0131 D1 a pre-18 bare (organization_id, COLUMN) unique composite proposes no tightening at all — it is the plain composite new DDL declares (sql-driver-unique-tenancy.test.ts › 'bare composite from a pre-18 database — no tightening proposed (ADR-0131 D1)') — so duplicate NULL-organization rows under it are no blocker and stage nothing here

`autoMigrate` is honoured by the native sqlite / postgres / mysql drivers only — the sqlite-wasm driver is constructed without it (the guidance entry on SqliteWasmConfigSchema says writing it there changes nothing), and turso's config declares no such key (standalone-stack.ts). Do not stage the wasm/turso arms expecting behavior

variants: off — the driver default when the key is omitted (sql-driver.ts `autoMigrate ?? 'off'`): drift is WARNED, never applied

safe — the safe-category subset applied at boot (the clean-probe replacement of a legacy platform-wide unique index, a missing declared index, dropping a runtime-token column default, widening a varchar on dialects that enforce length — not sqlite), never needs_confirm or destructive DDL: relaxing a NOT NULL column is needs_confirm and is never auto-applied

dev injection — `os dev`/`os serve --dev` pass 'safe' themselves for the FALLBACK default datasource (storage-driver.ts) and the telemetry datasource (serve.ts); non-dev serve passes nothing, so the driver default 'off' stands
NODE_ENV=production — 'safe' force-ignored with the named warning, schema never auto-altered
schemaMode gate — safe is honoured only under schemaMode 'managed' (sql-driver.ts autoOn = safe && managed); an external-schema datasource is never auto-altered

duplicates-blocked — a unique create_index goes through the ADR-0120 D4 duplicate pre-flight probe (sql-driver.ts applyNullSafeUniquePreflight): clean → the create proceeds, duplicates → BLOCKED with a row report and an applyLimit, created neither by `os migrate apply` nor by a safe boot. The bare → NULL-safe tighten that probe once recategorised safe is no longer proposed since ADR-0131 D1
steps: stage three drifts in the scratch copy, one per category: (1) needs_confirm — declare a field with `storage: { notNull: true }` (`required: true` no longer makes a NOT NULL column, ADR-0113), build, boot once against the file DB so the NOT NULL column lands, stop, drop the storage constraint and build: relax_not_null is needs_confirm, so it is the warn-only specimen on every boot; (2) safe — give a field `unique: true` (the boot lands the tenant-scoped uniq_TABLE_organization_id_COLUMN index), then with the server STOPPED plant the legacy platform-wide index on the scratch file: CREATE UNIQUE INDEX TABLE_COLUMN_unique ON TABLE(COLUMN) — the replace_unique_index drift, safe after a clean duplicate probe; (3) destructive — remove a field from metadata. Dump the scratch file's schema (sqlite_master for the table) before every boot below

the off side first: boot with the datasource's config carrying `autoMigrate: 'off'` (and once more with the key OMITTED — the driver default); capture the [schema-drift] WARNING for each of the three divergences in both boots and confirm the schema dump before/after the two boots is identical. ⚠ `os migrate plan` is not the pending oracle here: with the primary on a config-declared datasource it composes no driver for it and prints a PARTIAL plan ('Examined 0 managed table(s)', 'N of N declared object(s) are NOT … bound to no driver'), so the next boot's warning plus the dump stands in for it

the safe side: boot the same DB with `autoMigrate: 'safe'`; capture the `[schema-drift] auto-reconciled replace_unique_index on TABLE.COLUMN` info line and confirm the dump lost the legacy index, while the relax_not_null and orphaned-column warnings still print; boot AGAIN and confirm no further reconcile lines (the heal converged)

production force-off: re-plant the legacy index, then boot with NODE_ENV=production and `autoMigrate: 'safe'` still declared; capture the exact warning `[schema-drift] autoMigrate='safe' is ignored under NODE_ENV=production — schema is never auto-altered in production. Run 'os migrate' deliberately.` and confirm via schema dump that nothing was altered

the injected arm: in a scratch project with NO config-declared datasource (os dev -d file:HOST_DB), boot once, stop, plant the same legacy index in that file and boot plain `os dev` — the default datasource carries autoMigrate:'safe' on a dev boot (devAutoMigrateConfig, packages/runtime/src/dev-auto-migrate.ts — the one decision createStandaloneStack's default datasource and the CLI's config-load fallback both read since #21733), so the same auto-reconciled line must appear with no authored key anywhere; then re-plant it and boot non-dev `os start` over the same file — warnings only, the index stays

the destructive and needs_confirm boundary on the same boots: the removed field (orphaned column, destructive) and the relaxed NOT NULL (needs_confirm) stay warnings on every safe boot — `os migrate apply` (with --allow-destructive for the drop) remains the only door (cross-ref cli.migrate-plan-apply-json)

the duplicates-blocked leg: run the unit pins (packages/drivers/driver-sql/src/sql-driver-25031-blocked-unique-apply-limit.test.ts, and sql-driver-unique-tenancy.test.ts's ADR-0131 D1 no-tightening describe) and cite their output; for the safe-boot half, hand-stage it: with the server STOPPED, write two rows sharing one value of a field into the scratch sqlite file, give that field `unique: true`, build, boot with safe, and capture the BLOCKED report while the schema dump still has no index on it; record which route each half rests on

acceptance.clause: `safe` applies EXACTLY the safe-categorized diffs at boot and reports each one: every applied op logs `[schema-drift] auto-reconciled <op.type> on <table>.<column>` (info), drift is re-detected after the reconcile, and anything remaining is still warned once per divergence — never silently swallowed
acceptance.verify: the safe boot's log carries one auto-reconciled line per staged safe-category drift and none for the needs_confirm or destructive ones; the dump lost the legacy index; a second safe boot reconciles nothing (converged). Mechanism: reconcileAndWarnDrift filters category === 'safe' into applyMigrationEntries({ allowDestructive: false }) (sql-driver.ts)
acceptance.evidence: the boot log lines + the before/after schema dumps

acceptance.clause: `off` — explicit OR omitted — boots WITHOUT touching the schema: the same drift is warned (`[schema-drift] <message>`) on every boot, two consecutive off boots report identical drift, and the physical schema is byte-identical before and after
acceptance.verify: paired boot logs show the warnings both times with no auto-reconciled line; the schema dumps match exactly. The default is 'off' at the DRIVER (sql-driver.ts) — only the CLI's dev boots inject 'safe'
acceptance.evidence: the two boot logs + the schema-dump pair

acceptance.clause: production force-off: with NODE_ENV=production, a declared `autoMigrate: 'safe'` is IGNORED with the exact named warning and the remedy ('Run os migrate deliberately') — the schema is never auto-altered in production, whatever the config says
acceptance.verify: the production boot log carries the sql-driver.ts warning verbatim and NO auto-reconciled line; the schema dump is unchanged
acceptance.evidence: the warning line + the unchanged schema dump

acceptance.clause: the gate composes: safe runs only under schemaMode 'managed' (autoOn = autoMigrate==='safe' && schemaMode==='managed'), and the DESTRUCTIVE category is never auto-applied under any setting — a staged drop stays a warning + pending plan entry on the safe boot, applied only through `os migrate apply --allow-destructive`
acceptance.verify: the safe boot's log shows the drop (and the needs_confirm relax) warned, not applied, and the next boot warns them again; the applyMigrationEntries call is pinned allowDestructive:false (sql-driver.ts)
acceptance.evidence: the safe-boot logs + the dump still carrying the orphaned column

acceptance.clause: a unique index the stored rows already violate fails CLOSED: the ADR-0120 D4 duplicate pre-flight probe BLOCKS the create_index — category destructive, an applyLimit naming the conflicting group, a row report in its message — and no index is created, under either autoMigrate value and even by an allowDestructive apply; and since ADR-0131 D1 a pre-18 bare (organization_id, COLUMN) composite is the plain composite new DDL declares, so it proposes no tightening: zero drift, the index and any duplicate NULL-organization rows kept
acceptance.verify: run the pinning suites and cite their output: sql-driver-25031-blocked-unique-apply-limit.test.ts (the plain and organization-scoped blocked entries, the refused allowDestructive apply, and the duplicate-free CONTROL that creates the index) and sql-driver-unique-tenancy.test.ts › 'bare composite from a pre-18 database — no tightening proposed (ADR-0131 D1)' (its zero-drift safe boot and its no-op over duplicate NULL-organization rows). Neither boots a safe driver over the blocked create, so that half is steps[6]'s hand-staged capture; name which route each half rests on
acceptance.evidence: the test output (or the staged blocked report)

acceptance.clause: one decision injects 'safe' ONLY on a dev boot and only for the SQL kinds whose connection contract declares autoMigrate (sqlite, postgres, mysql): devAutoMigrateConfig, read by the standalone stack's default datasource, the CLI's config-load fallback and the telemetry sibling datasource — so a plain `os dev` self-heals with no authored key, while a production `os serve` boot leaves the driver at its own 'off' default
acceptance.verify: the keyless dev boot shows the auto-reconciled line (injection worked); a non-dev serve boot over the same staged drift shows warnings only (packages/runtime/src/dev-auto-migrate.ts devAutoMigrateConfig: `dev && DEV_AUTO_MIGRATE_DRIVERS.has(driver) ? { autoMigrate: 'safe' } : {}`, spread by standalone-stack.ts, storage-driver.ts resolveStorageDefinition and telemetry-datasource.ts — never an inline isDev branch of their own)
